boundaries.label: Feature slices — WALL: a feature never imports another feature's internals
Core — domain (pure JVM) + data + Room · WALL: domain has no android.*, Room, Retrofit or Hilt
Platform — Android capability adapters behind ports · never consumes feature UI

cards.title: The module graph is the law
items: domain modules apply the Kotlin/JVM plugin, not the Android plugin — an android.* import there does not compile
a module's dependencies {} is the complete list of what it may import, so a forbidden edge is a compile error rather than a review comment
the consumer declares the port and the data or platform module implements it: SessionStore and TokenProvider by the domain, Navigator and PermissionChecker by the feature ui
ports return domain types; no android.* type ever crosses into the domain

cards.title: Variants and the feature wall
items: :apps:game, :apps:market and :apps:avatar are thin app modules over shared feature and core modules; the market app does not depend on the game engine or its permissions
one variant = one application module = one binary; a product flavor that merely hides code is not the architecture
a feature importing another feature's internals is a Must fix — the Gradle dependency graph is the wall, and the fix is to re-cut the layout

cards.title: The enforcement map
items: domain has no android.* → a JVM-only module plus a forbidden-import check
feature UI does not import another feature's internals → the Gradle dependency graph
the app module contains no business logic → review plus the module graph
no main-thread I/O → StrictMode plus the detekt coroutine rules; no secret outside the Keystore → review plus a detekt and security scan

cards.title: Exceptions are re-cuts
items: when a change would cross a layer, re-cut the layout: move the logic to the module that owns it
the rule is never to weaken or delete the lints to make a change pass; a config exception is a contract change, and a module-wide @Suppress is a finding
the lint config lives once, in lints/detekt.yml and lints/.editorconfig — when the skill and the config disagree, the config wins and the skill is fixed
